exemplar.title: What strong work looks like
exemplar.intro: Here is how a lead robotics engineer explains purchasing and storage decisions, so you can see the moves, not the answers.

traits.sample: I divided 620 chassis bolts by 24 bolts per organizer bin to get 25 remainder 20. Because the 20 remaining bolts cannot be left loose on the workbench, I ordered 26 bins so all hardware is protected.
traits.why: Naming the quotient and explaining what the remainder means shows deep division sense and earns top marks.

traits.sample: I shifted decimals two places to turn $78.75 ÷ $3.75 into 7875 ÷ 375 = 21 sensor packs. Multiplying by a power of 10 keeps the quotient equivalent.
traits.why: Showing the power-of-10 shift proves the algorithm was understood conceptually, not guessed.

traits.trait: Connects math to the real decision
traits.sample: For the ribbon cable, dividing 15 meters by 5/8 meter gave 15 × (8/5) = 24 harnesses. Dividing by a fraction smaller than 1 produces more pieces than wholes.
traits.why: Connecting the reciprocal to piece size justifies why division creates more pieces.

traits.sample: I checked reasonableness: 620 is close to 600, and 600 ÷ 24 = 25, so 26 bins is extremely reasonable.
traits.why: Estimation checks catch computation errors and show expert number sense.
